newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech group says c.bank knew of failed debt scheme.
newsitem.headline: Czech group says c.bank knew of failed debt scheme.

text.p: A group connected to Kreditni Banka a.s., the largest failed Czech bank, said on Monday that a debt-transfer scheme for which four suspects have been indicted was approved by the Czech National Bank (CNB).

On Friday, five former Kreditni executives, including two connected with the Czech investment group Motoinvest, were arrested on charges of fraud which caused losses totalling at least 2.88 billion crowns ($109 million) ($108.6 million).

One of the executives from investment group Motoinvest, which burst onto Czech headlines last year with a series of takeover battles against big institutions, was later released for lack of evidence, but one remained in jail on fraud charges.
The head of Motoinvest, Pavel Tykac, called a news conference on Monday to say the plan for which his colleague David Knop-Kostka remained under indictment had had the blessing of the central bank.
"The operation was done in consultation with the CNB...which marked it as a standard solution to (Kreditni's) bad loans," Tykac said.

CNB spokesman Martin Svehla was not immediately available for comment, but he was quoted by the Czech agency CTK as saying that the CNB had known of the plan but had cited two auditors' statements which called it potentially risky.
Svehla was not quoted about the criminality of such a plan.
The licence for Kreditni, in which Motoinvest held shares for a brief period in 1994, was withdrawn by the CNB in August with losses estimated at nearly 12 billion crowns.

The failure of Kreditni, a medium-sized bank based in the western city of Plzen, caused a political furore and led the government to create a special commission of ministers to lead an investigation into the case.
Kreditni's collapse meant that the firms at the end of the scheme, AB Real and Lexus, had lost their 2.88 billion crown investment.

Knop-Kostka, who was responsible for financial transactions at Kreditni, along with the bank's former general director, his deputy, and an executive secretary, are facing charges of fraud, damage to creditors and abetting fraud.
